subject.title: Feature: Sleep/wait tool — agent can pause execution without burning tokens

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class core `sleep` self-pause tool, and should its delay cap and resume semantics be a dedicated gateway primitive or a cron-backed session-targeted implementation?
rationale: The request changes core agent turn scheduling, model-facing tools, session continuation, and possibly config/sandbox policy, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product and API semantics.

options.title: Sponsor a core sleep primitive
options.body: Accept the capability and require the implementation to prove same-session resume, user-interrupt cancellation, cap enforcement, and restart non-durability.

options.title: Keep existing cron/process guidance
options.body: Reject a new default tool for now and keep cron wakes, process completion wakes, and `sessions_yield` as the supported waiting surfaces.

options.title: Narrow to an extension seam
options.body: Ask for a plugin/runtime API seam instead of bundling a default core tool if maintainers want optional scheduling behavior outside core.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a core sleep primitive
recommendation.body: Accept the capability and require the implementation to prove same-session resume, user-interrupt cancellation, cap enforcement, and restart non-durability.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans product direction and core agent/gateway runtime surfaces where steipete is both listed project owner and recent area contributor.
